sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Lowe’s Companies (LOW) climbed 25.7% between October 6 and November 4, 2026, yet the stock still trades below the median S&P 500 company’s multiple. The stock trades at 19.3 times earnings, compared with 22.9 for the median company. This discount could mark a sound retailer on sale, or a fair price for a business with a real problem. So what does a buyer get from Lowe’s for that lower multiple?

A buyer gets a home improvement retailer whose sales are growing again. Revenue rose 8.2% over the twelve months ended July 31, 2026, following declines in each of the prior three twelve-month periods, though comparable sales grew far less in the latest quarter. Management said strong performance in Pro, Online and Home Services helped offset softer spending by do-it-yourself customers in the quarter ended July 31, 2026. Online sales grew 15.7% during that quarter.

Lowe’s also turns those sales into cash. The company generated $7.0 billion of free cash flow over the twelve months ended July 31, 2026, delivering a 5.5% yield on its market value. This cash more than covered the $2.69 billion it paid in dividends over the same twelve months. A buyer also pays 15.8% less per dollar of earnings than for the median S&P 500 company.

Lowe’s earned $2.4 billion of net income in the quarter ended July 31, 2026, the same as a year earlier, on an 8.3% increase in sales. Comparable sales rose just 0.2% for the quarter. On an August 19, 2026 call, management said discretionary DIY demand remains under pressure. Management also said the FBM and ADG acquisitions diluted its gross margin that quarter.

The longer record shows the same strain. Net income fell in each of the last two twelve-month periods, dropping to $6.64 billion in the twelve months ended July 31, 2026 from $6.93 billion two years earlier. Operating margin stood at 11.4% over the latest twelve months, below its 12.1% average across the last three twelve-month periods, which includes the latest.
The discount is to the market, not to Lowe’s own history. At the end of June in each of the last three years, Lowe’s stock traded at 18.1 to 18.6 times earnings, sitting below where it trades now.

sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Lowe’s Companies (LOW) have climbed 19.6% since October 5, 2026, outpacing a 2.6% loss for the S&P 500. Earlier, in August, management cut its full-year 2026 sales outlook to about $92 billion, down from $93 billion, to reflect current consumer demand and housing trends. Below are the events most likely to move Lowe’s stock over the next six months. Which of them matters most for Lowe’s shareholders?

Lowe’s own third-quarter report, expected in November 2026, matters most because it is the first set of results since management lowered its outlook. The earnings calendar lists the release for November 18, before the market opens. For the quarter, management guided to comparable sales in line with a roughly flat full year, alongside adjusted earnings per share about 7% below a year earlier. Management also said spending on do-it-yourself projects remains under pressure. Against that guide, comparable sales and adjusted earnings per share are the measures to watch when Lowe’s reports in November 2026.

Management expects weak home building to keep pressing on Lowe’s through the second half of fiscal 2026. The pressure falls on two businesses Lowe’s bought to win larger professional customers: Foundation Building Materials, acquired for $8.8 billion in October 2025, and Artisan Design Group, which installs flooring, cabinets and countertops for home builders. Elevated mortgage rates continue to suppress new home construction, hurting both sales and profit at the two businesses, management said. The acquisitions also diluted gross margin in the quarter ended July 2026, management said, so gross margin is the measure to watch in November 2026.

Competitors cut prices on grills, patio and live goods in July 2026, and management said those rivals paid for the cuts with tariff refunds. Lowe’s chose not to match some of those promotions. The July results showed the impact, management said, with comparable sales falling 1.2% that month. A shift in the timing of the July 4 holiday also took about 75 basis points off July’s comparable sales, management said.

Chad Lowe’s Latest Life Change Comes After a Devastating Year
sum: Actor Chad Lowe and his wife, Kim Painter, are selling their house in Los Angeles. The home sale comes shortly after the loss of their middle daughter, Fiona Lowe, at the age of 13.

TMZ reports that according to real estate records they reviewed, the home located in the Mar Vista area was put on the market on October 16. TMZ also indicates that Lowe and Painter have accepted an offer on the property, although the media outlet indicates there are contingencies incorporated into the offer.

The family purchased the home in March 2025. The house has 3,239 square feet of living space, which includes four bedrooms and three bathrooms. The family purchased the home for $3.15 million, and the current offer they accepted is for $3.249 million, according to TMZ.

The decision to sell their home comes after a couple of incredibly difficult years. Not only did Lowe and Painter lose their daughter Fiona in September, but they also lost their previous house to a wildfire in January 2025.
In February 2025, Lowe shared a heart-wrenching photo on his Instagram page showing what was left of their former home.

They lost the house in the January 2025 wildfires that ravaged the area. He noted in his February post that it was the first time his three daughters were seeing what used to be their home since they evacuated a month earlier.
Lowe wrote, "The way they've handled this whole devastating experience is nothing short of remarkable. I am in awe of their spirit and resilience."

Home Depot's strategy emphasizes product innovation, Pro engagement and omnichannel convenience. Its AI-powered Magic Apron enhances customer assistance, while nationwide express delivery offers fulfillment within three hours. sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Lowe’s (LOW) stock lost 17.2% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 16.5%. You probably think of Lowe’s as a store for do-it-yourself homeowners, and management says those shoppers are holding back. But management also says two acquisitions position Lowe’s to win more business from larger professional contractors, its Pro customers. Buyers at today’s price may be betting on that. So is Lowe’s Pro business still growing while homeowners hold back?
Yes, so far: Management said Pro delivered another quarter of growth in the quarter ended July 31, 2026. Lowe’s posted $26 billion in total sales for the quarter, up 8.3% from a year earlier.

Pro did not grow alone. Management said Online and Home Services, which serves customers who want the job done for them, joined Pro in helping offset softer do-it-yourself spending. Online sales grew 15.7%.

Lowe’s has also put money behind Pro. Management says FBM and ADG, two acquired businesses that sell into residential construction, position the company to grow its share with larger Pro customers over the long term.
Not yet. Lowe’s earned $2.4 billion in the quarter ended July 31, 2026. That matched its earnings from a year earlier on $2.0 billion more in sales.

Its operating margin slipped to 13.7% from 14.5% a year earlier. Management said gross margin was 80 basis points below the prior year’s adjusted figure. That drop included the dilutive impact of the FBM and ADG acquisitions, which suggests the businesses Lowe’s bought to reach Pro customers earn thinner margins than the rest of the company.

Why Are Investors Discounting The High Cash Yield On Lowe’s Stock?
sum: Shares of Lowe’s Companies (LOW) sit about 37% below their February 2026 high. That decline has lifted the retailer’s cash yield. Free cash flow equals 7.0% of the company’s market value as of October 6, 2026, compared with 4.5% for the median S&P 500 company. This gap suggests one of two scenarios: either the stock is a bargain, or the market expects Lowe’s to generate less cash going forward. So why are investors paying so little for the cash Lowe’s produces?

Lowe’s generates nearly all its cash from a single business: home improvement retail. The segment accounted for 97% of revenue in fiscal 2025, which ended January 30, 2026. This cash production matters because it ultimately belongs to shareholders, whether the company distributes it or retains it. Once investors recognize that underlying value, the share price tends to follow.
Over the last twelve months, Lowe’s generated $9.3 billion from operations and spent $2.3 billion on capital projects. That combination left the company with $7.0 billion in free cash flow.

This cash generation has largely held steady over the past three years, despite a recent dip. Free cash flow stood at $6.6 billion three years ago and grew to $7.6 billion two years ago. The metric reached $7.7 billion a year ago before slipping to the current $7.0 billion. Through all 13 rolling twelve-month periods during that timeframe, free cash flow remained positive.

Lenders also have a claim on a portion of that cash. The company carries $38.8 billion of net debt, which equals 38.6% of its market value. When measured against the combined total of market value and debt, the resulting cash yield is 5.0%. Even with this debt load, the company’s operating profit covers its interest bill 6.4 times.

Investors may doubt the cash because profit margins have narrowed and management has lowered its forecast for the year. During the fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call on August 19, 2026, management cut its full-year sales forecast to $92 billion, the low end of its earlier range of $92 billion to $94 billion.

While total sales in the second quarter rose 8.3% from a year earlier, comparable sales grew only 0.2%. At the same time, the operating margin over the last twelve months fell to 11.4%, down from 12.4% a year ago.

Catherine Giudici Shares Update After Son’s Diabetes Diagnosis: ‘Getting Used to This New Normal’
sum: The Bachelor’s Catherine Giudici is thanking fans for their support after her and husband Sean Lowe’s son Isaiah was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes.

“This week, we found our strength,” Giudici, 40, wrote via Instagram on Sunday, July 26. “It came in the form of texts, gifts, cards, people, each other, God. Thank you to all the friends and loved ones who lifted us up when we needed it, and [we are] so grateful for the foundation we built as a family before this.”

Giudici also shared an update on Isaiah, 8, noting that he is “doing better” following his hospitalization last week and is “getting used to this new normal and reeeeally getting used to being spoiled 🤣.”

Along with her update, Giudici shared photos of the gifts and cards they received from friends and family. One snap showed several children’s books centered on T1D and a laser arcade game, while others featured signs reading, “You’ve got this, Isaiah” and “We love you, Isaiah.”
Giudici and Lowe, 42, first revealed Isaiah’s health battle on Tuesday, July 21.

“This past week has been a rough one for the Lowes. Our precious boy Isaiah was admitted to Children’s Hospital and diagnosed with type 1 diabetes,” Giudici wrote via Instagram at the time. “Our wonderful pediatrician noticed some symptoms at our annual appointment that stuck out to her.”

She continued, “He had lost 11 pounds since his last visit (we thought he just had a growth spurt) and had been drinking and peeing A LOT (it’s really hot here in the summer). Otherwise healthy and active, she ran some tests and sent us to the emergency room based on those alarming results. Thankful for the nurses, doctors and staff who gave us a four-year college education on his condition in four days.”

sum: Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW) closed down by 3.50%. The Retailers sector is down by 1.04%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) down 0.91%; Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) down 0.50%; Home Depot Inc (HD) down 2.54%.

The downward movement in Lowe's share price today is primarily driven by a convergence of macroeconomic headwinds and softening indicators within the broader housing market. As a company deeply tethered to the health of the residential real estate sector, Lowe's is experiencing heightened sensitivity to recent data suggesting a slowdown in home turnover. Elevated mortgage rates continue to act as a deterrent for potential homebuyers, which in turn reduces the immediate demand for the significant home improvement projects and appliance upgrades that typically follow a home sale.

From an industry perspective, there is growing evidence of a shift in consumer spending patterns. Recent retail data indicates that middle-income households, a core demographic for the home improvement giant, are increasingly prioritizing essential expenditures over discretionary DIY projects. This deceleration in the do-it-yourself segment is particularly impactful for Lowe's, which historically maintains a higher proportion of DIY customers compared to its primary competitors. The market is currently pricing in the risk that this pullback in consumer spending may be more prolonged than initially forecasted.

Institutional sentiment has also been dampened by broader volatility across the consumer discretionary sector. Analysts have noted that while the company has made strides in expanding its professional contractor business, the current high-interest-rate environment makes it difficult to offset the weakness in the retail consumer base. Furthermore, the volatility observed during the trading session suggests a broader de-risking strategy among institutional investors who are rotating out of interest-rate-sensitive equities in favor of more defensive positions amidst uncertainty regarding the Federal Reserve's next move.
Operational risks related to margin pressure are also weighing on the stock.

The Trade Desk Stock Is Down 47% This Year. Here’s What Has to Be True for It to Come Back
sum: The Drawdown Chart for TTD Is Unlike Anything Else in This Market

Most stocks in 2026 have had rough patches. The Trade Desk (TTD) has had a freefall. The stock entered the year already well off its highs, then kept going lower through January, February, March, April, May, and June without ever finding a floor that held.

The drawdowns chart is a staircase going in one direction. A brief bounce to around -25% in early March was the closest thing to a recovery all year, and even that gave back within weeks. The maximum drawdown hit 56.79% on June 25, and the stock currently sits at -50.76% from its year-start level.

From its all-time high area near $91 last summer, the stock has now lost roughly 75% of its value. The causes stack up: revenue growth decelerated from 25% in Q1 2025 to 12% in Q1 2026, the Chief Revenue Officer was pushed out after just seven months on the job, Publicis, one of the world’s largest advertising agency groups, pulled back from recommending The Trade Desk to its clients during a months-long dispute over alleged hidden ad fees and failed audits.

This dispute has since been resolved, and the two parties have issued a joint statement saying they are moving forward, but the damage to sentiment was real. Amazon has also been gaining ground in programmatic advertising, raising structural questions about whether The Trade Desk can maintain its independent positioning against a platform that controls both the pipes and the inventory.
A new CFO was appointed on July 9, and HSBC upgraded the stock to Hold from Reduce last week, both modest but genuine signals that the worst of the news flow may be passing.
Whatever the market is pricing in for The Trade Desk, it is not a declining business. Revenue has grown every single year since the company went public.

items.t: Lowe's Companies Inc Stock (LOW) Moved Down by 3.23% on Jul 8: What Signal Does It Send?
sum: Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW) moved down by 3.23%. The Retailers sector is down by 1.35%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) down 1.67%; Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) up 0.69%; Home Depot Inc (HD) down 2.72%.

The downward movement in Lowe's Companies shares during today’s session is primarily driven by a sharp escalation in geopolitical tensions. The sudden end of the temporary United States-Iran ceasefire triggered a massive surge in international oil prices, sparking renewed fears of sticky inflation across the global economy. As West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude jumped, the broader market experienced a pronounced risk-off turn, dragging down major equity indices and hitting consumer cyclical sectors particularly hard.

For highly rate-sensitive consumer discretionary businesses like home improvement, this geopolitical shock has severe implications. The spike in energy prices immediately pushed the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield higher. A rising bond yield is highly correlated with a corresponding rise in mortgage rates. The prospect of prolonged, elevated borrowing costs threatens to further freeze the domestic real estate market. Given that home improvement demand is heavily dependent on housing turnover and home equity-driven renovations, a renewed chill in the real estate sector severely dampens investor optimism regarding Lowe’s short-term growth prospects.

The macro-driven sell-off was compounded by newly updated housing industry projections. A prominent midyear real estate forecast revised home price growth expectations downward to a rate trailing projected inflation, signaling that home values are declining in real terms. This cooling of home price appreciation, coupled with a lowered forecast for existing-home sales, points to a sluggish environment for big-ticket retail. While Lowe's has demonstrated resilient execution in recent quarters and has actively sought to gain market share with its professional contractor push, a flat home improvement backdrop means discretionary upgrades from average do-it-yourself shoppers will likely remain depressed.
